title: Tightey Whiteys
summary: Chapter 12 is an 82-minute ensemble episode about Steve Lee's continued employment, Mangchi rehearsal, Poon's old art, PURPS/RVCA and Luke Davis, fan recognition, an explicitly visual ‘tighty-whiteys’ costume, wrestling, a Sasha Grey party, chew-and-spit behavior, social-media craft, trivia and Mangchi performances. The cleaner reduces 2,479 raw segments to 2,276 clean segments and about 14,874 raw words to 14,839 clean words through 210 recorded edits. That mechanical reduction does not constitute the finished transcript. The reviewed correction layer adds 386 ordered decisions, repairs public entities, isolates missing/indistinct spans, and preserves consent and health chronology that a fluent rewrite could otherwise erase. The opening is Mangchi's officially cataloged ‘When the Bullies Fall,’ not generic violent speech, but several lyrics remain non-quotation-grade. Steve reports a temporary neck tattoo, shower routine, weight/cardio goals and a seven-post Instagram assignment inside the same employment conversation that follows his last paycheck and proposal to remain at Igloo Hong Enterprises. The appearance and social-post expectations therefore carry employer/bandleader power, even where Steve agrees or values the coaching. A long anal-penetration threat must not be summarized as banter. Steve says ‘please don't,’ ‘I would rather die,’ ‘if you were to rape me,’ ‘no, I don't,’ and repeats that the assault would make him suicidal. David's claim that Steve wants it or says yes with his eyes is directly contradicted by those words. The Golden Gate Bridge sequence invokes *The Bridge*, a Christ Air, survival, paralysis and a second threatened assault in a hospital. It remains in full with suicide and disability warnings, not operational detail or romanticized survival lore. Mangchi rehearsal repairs ‘Gook Boy’ and preserves the performed slur/alienation lyrics with uncertain words marked rather than invented. Poon's charcoal drawings and printed shirts are important visual/creative evidence: he once wanted to be a comic-book artist, uses a peace-activist design and discusses a shirt derived from the 1968 Olympics Black Power salute. Video is required to identify the designs and logo text. Product/event repairs include PURPS, RVCA, Billabong and Estevan Oriol. The claimed sale price is an unverified estimate. RVCA independently verifies Luke Davis as a Capo Beach surfer; the room's Ryan Gosling/James Dean comparisons, sexual orientation question, private-life speculation and sexualization remain attributed opinions, not biography or consent. A mother/teenage-daughter fantasy is excluded from neutral discovery. The appearance-strategy discussion—conventional beauty versus purple-haired distinction—is retained as a creative-image argument. The episode title is inseparable from video. Steve's garment is repeatedly called Fruit of the Loom and tighty-whiteys, but participants also describe rubber, skin, paint-on latex, visible genitals and a final painful removal. Audio cannot establish its actual material. The editorial record therefore marks every body/costume turn as video-dependent instead of falsely normalizing it to ordinary underwear. When David asks to get behind Steve or penetrate him, Steve repeatedly says no and please don't. A ten-second limit, friendship, prior touch or a future moment ‘when your defenses are down’ does not create consent; the sleep-related threat heightens the concern. Asa's underwear and Steve's consensually discussed smell/masturbation routine remain explicit source content, but Asa's response to that particular discussion does not authorize unrelated acts. The Spanish edition of her memoir is repaired to *Sólo para adultos*, and the film to *Asa Akira Is Insatiable 2* with Nacho Vidal. Val's discussion of recognition shows unequal public-contact burdens: he enjoys some encounters, Asa dislikes recognition around her parents, and David objects when autograph requests turn into demands for more free art. Those boundaries remain person- and context-specific. The Sasha Grey party recap includes James Jean's return, food, rain, Kevin Hayes, Saelee Oh and a wrestling game. Friendship cannot be awarded or deleted by a match. Steve's Poway wrestling history and second-in-California claim remain first-person, not independently verified achievement. Genital-contact suggestions, sweep-the-leg calls and costume exposure require video and act-specific consent. The party's fecal-stunt chronology is preserved without euphemism. Saelee reportedly jokes twice that Steve may defecate on her chest, while Steve repeatedly says he has no desire to do it. The group pressures him for about an hour and frames completion as making the party epic. When he removes his pants and tries, he says Saelee pushes him away and says ‘stop, stop.’ The room then suggests she would get up if she truly objected and dismisses the stop as unreal. Those are false consent tests. A verbal invitation does not waive a later stop or physical resistance; joking, prank history, diarrhea, other guests' encouragement and a host's general reaction cannot authorize contact. No feces is produced, but the attempted contact and later reenactments remain meaningful. The improved transcript keeps invitation, doubt, pushing, stop, minimization and outcome together. It does not convert fecal contamination, deliberate dietary buildup or anal touching into instructions. David's repeated chew-and-spit account is a health signal: he says he is becoming addicted to it, spits chewed steak and desserts into napkins and treats smoothies/vegetables as making the pattern acceptable. The record preserves the behavior but does not present it as weight-control advice or medically harmless. The room's meal contains several possible gas triggers, so no single food is diagnosed as causal. Diarrhea and E. coli statements remain self-report/speculation, with handwashing and surface-contamination concerns retained. The social-media section contains a useful craft distinction. Steve is funny and generative in person and can write interesting Mangchi songs with Money Mark, yet his feed shows context-free objects. A humorous diner/Tinder story works because it frames an event; an exciting feed can also manufacture excitement from an ordinary life. The coaching to tell real stories, ask open questions and text as if speaking to a person is preserved, while private women, phone numbers and messages stay protected and the one-post-per-day assignment remains connected to employment power. Trivia repairs Poway, Ralphs, Inglewood, Azusa, Hollywood, Oakland and Pasadena, but racial/antisemitic guesses do not become metadata. The anal-smell game closes with several refusals and a correct contamination concern: touching the anus can transfer fecal germs to hands and shared surfaces. Macau brotherhood is not permission. The closing retailer is Ross Dress for Less, the claimed brand is Fruit of the Loom, and the final song is Mangchi's ‘Reverse Birthday.’ The last ‘Mercury’ passage remains unresolved performance audio. No viewpoint or difficult idea is censored. Privacy, medical, safety and discovery annotations govern presentation; they do not rewrite the source. No named line-level dialogue publishes because the episode has zero held-out identity windows and zero acoustically validated turns.

connections.note: The last paycheck, continued-employment proposal, body/cardio target, song memorization and daily-post assignment keep creative coaching inside an employer-controlled structure.
The opening song turns bullying into violent revenge imagery and requires performance context rather than literal dialogue indexing.
Rehearsal tests whether Steve has memorized a song whose racialized alienation story remains partly obscured by musical ASR.
The official title repairs the closing generic Birthday transcript and connects the episode to later music-video material.
Repeated no, please don't and rape language directly contradict body-language claims and ten-second bargaining.
The assault hypothetical escalates into Golden Gate Bridge performance, documentary reference, survival lore and disability threat.
Charcoal work, comic-book ambition and shirt designs expand Poon beyond recurring sexual/trivia material.
One Poon shirt is explicitly explained through the raised-fist image, though video is needed to evaluate the design.
The Orange County trip combines friendship trickery, a drink launch and a corrected RVCA/Billabong ownership story.
RVCA corroborates the surfing identity while the episode's beauty, orientation and private-life talk remains attributed speculation.
The garment/body-paint/latex question, exposure, wrestling and painful removal cannot be resolved from audio.
The verified Spanish memoir title repairs a repeated partial title and ties recognition to parental boundaries.
The film and Nacho Vidal repairs anchor Val's account of showing the work to a private friend.
Val's enjoyment, Asa's parent-specific discomfort and David's escalating autograph demands demonstrate different public-access contracts.
The gathering joins food, hosting, returning artist, wrestling, bodily games and pressure around a proposed fecal stunt.
Reported joking invitations are followed by pushing away and stop; the later refusal controls despite prank history or audience pressure.
David's addiction language and repeated restaurant/hotel routine make the episode a health signal, not a dieting tutorial.
Steve can rapidly turn prompts into songs even while struggling to translate that interest into social-post storytelling.
The diner post, context-free skateboard image and manufactured exciting feeds form a compact lesson in narrative framing.
The late game tests immediate recall, geographic nicknames and how jokes can become false event history.
Poon shirts, temporary tattoo, purple hair, poncho, wrestling, costume exposure, reenactments and removal all require YouTube/video recovery.

CDC says human feces can carry Salmonella, E. coli O157 and norovirus, can contaminate hands and surfaces, and should be addressed with soap-and-water handwashing: https://www.cdc.gov/clean-hands/data-research/facts-stats/index.html

The closing repeated *Mercury* material, the extra band influence around 691, several performed lyrics, the Poon shirt logo, Old Spice product line and garment material remain audio/video-verification candidates.

The title sequence is fundamentally visual. Audio supplies conflicting descriptions—Fruit of the Loom, rubber, skin and paint-on latex—and a pain/removal sequence. Do not assert garment material until video is recovered.
Zero held-out identity windows and zero validated turns means no line-level speaker names. Episode-level cast familiarity cannot substitute for acoustic validation.
